Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with complaints of
neck and back pain consistent with soft tissue strain. Over the course of 20 visits,
care included manual therapy, targeted stretching, and supervised home exercise,
following a typical and expected treatment progression. Pain levels and range of
motion improved steadily, and visit frequency was gradually reduced as symptoms
resolved. Examination revealed palpable muscle guarding and reduced cervical and
lumbar rnage of motion, findings that support the reported injury, while neurological
screening and orthopedic special tests remained within normal limits. The mechanism of
injury is consistent with the clinical presentation. No prior complaints or treatment
involving the cervical or lumbar spine were reported in the patient's history. Billing
records reflect one charge per scheduled sevrice with no duplicate or repeated
entries. Prognosis is good with continued home exercise, and discharge from active
care is anticipated.
